text:
carla: Heads up — linkcheck failing on PR #4823. Looks like a link gets split after a fenced codeblock in the examples page.

docs-bot: [linkcheck] 1 broken external link: /examples/usage.html#sdk-snippet -> 404 (checked at 2026-02-19T14:02Z)

mike: ah i've seen this — docusaurus/mdx sometimes inserts a soft break if a code fence isn't followed by a blank line, then the anchor parser concatenates weirdly.

carla: reproduction: paste from built HTML. output shows this fragment:

```
<pre><code>client.generate(prompt)
```https://docs.redwood.inference/guides/sdk#generate

```

mike: yep — the closing triple backticks run into the url and the markdown->html serializer doesn't add a separator, so the linkchecker sees `...code>```https://...` and treats it as a path.

nora: i can push a fix: add an empty line after codeblock and wrap long urls in `< >` or put the URL on its own paragraph. which is preferred?

samir: prefer angle brackets `<https://docs.redwood.inference/guides/sdk#generate>` or put URL on its own paragraph. angle brackets are simplest and compatible with our markdown.

mike: also, add a tiny regression test in docs CI that renders the page and runs linkcheck on the built html to catch this class of bug. can be a single pytest that shells out to `mkdocs build` / `docusaurus build` and greps for concatenated code fences.

carla: cool. nora — can you include a short note in the PR description explaining why it's needed so future authors don't reintroduce it?

nora: yup — pushing a tiny patch in a sec. i'll follow up when green.

docs-bot: PR #4823 updated: linkcheck passed ✅ (after patch) — 2026-02-19T14:22Z :tada:

carla: thanks — leaving a comment to remind contributors about codeblock spacing in docs CONTRIBUTING.md :memo:

mike: LGTM

nora: done, thanks all :rocket:
